title: Security posture discovery with Atlas Financial
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options
summary: Discovery focused on Atlas Financial's security and compliance requirements. Primary concerns: SOC 2 evidence, SSO/SAML integration with Okta, fine-grained RBAC, audit log retention and export, envelope encryption and KMS control for dedicated/private, and data retention/erase policies for hosted API. Redwood AE/SE to share SOC2 report, network diagram for private deployment, SSO integration guide, and pricing for Dedicated capacity. Customer requested a technical deep dive and pilot benchmark on a non-prod dataset.

Tom Lin - Send SSO/SAML + SCIM integration guide and sample SAML metadata by 2025-09-05
Tom Lin - Prepare draft network architecture diagram for Redwood Private (VPC) and send by 2025-09-08
Maya Patel - Provide Dedicated capacity pricing and pilot terms by 2025-09-06
Marcus Lee (Atlas) - Provide non-prod sample dataset details and test SLA targets by 2025-09-10
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2, SAML guide, and network diagram (see action items)
Schedule technical deep dive with Atlas infra team week of 2025-09-15
Agree on pilot scope and success criteria (benchmarks for 99th pct latency and encryption key ownership)
Set up trial Dedicated queue for pilot if contract terms agreeable
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-02
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46 min
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Tom (Redwood SE), Jordan (Atlas - Head of Data), Priya (Atlas - Security Eng), Marcus (Atlas - Platform)

--- Auto-generated Summary (may be rough) ---
Maya: Quick security posture run-through, main ask is whether Redwood hosted can meet SOC2/data residency needs; Atlas leaning toward dedicated/private for key control.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on the account, and with me is Tom, our security and infra SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:10] Jordan: Good, thanks. We've been talking with a few vendors, want to see how Redwood stacks on the compliance front.
[00:00:18] Priya: Hi, I'm Priya. I'm going to focus on encryption, KMS, and audit trails.
[00:00:23] Marcus: Marcus here, I'll be looking at network, VPC, and deployment ops.
[00:00:28] Tom: Great, thanks. Quick agenda, we'll walk through SOC2/ISO posture, auth (SSO/SAML/SCIM), RBAC, audit logs, encryption and KMS options, and data retention. Then open Q&A.

[00:01:05] Jordan: High level first — Atlas is in finance, we need strong evidence of controls. SOC 2 Type II is required, and ISO 27001 would be a plus, and then we need to understand what is possible with hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:01:22] Maya: Totally. We are SOC 2 Type II compliant (recent attestation), and we can provide the report under NDA. For ISO, we dont currently have ISO 27001 cert but we map controls and can share our policies.
[00:01:36] Priya: When you say "hosted", does that mean Redwood has access to our keys? We can't have plaintext stored anywhere outside our control for PII.
[00:01:45] Tom: Good question. For hosted API we provide encryption at rest and in transit; keys are managed by Redwood KMS by default. For Dedicated or Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (CMK) via AWS KMS/HSM integrations so you can retain key ownership.
[00:02:02] Priya: Does customer-managed KMS apply to Dedicated only or also to Private?
[00:02:07] Tom: Both Dedicated and Private — Private gives you more control over the control plane and networking. In Dedicated we still run a Redwood-managed control plane but can configure CMK for data in the serving layer; for on-prem Private we can run the control plane in your environment and keys never leave your network.
[00:02:25] Marcus: For Private, what's the deployment model? Is it air-gapped supported?
[00:02:29] Tom: We have an on-prem package that can be deployed in air-gapped environments with an offline installer. There are a few manual steps for image signing and initial bootstrap, but it's supported.
[00:02:40] Marcus: Okay. Network wise, can we force all traffic through our VPC and control egress?
[00:02:44] Tom: Yes, for Private we run inside your VPC; for Dedicated we can peer or use private link options so traffic stays in your cloud boundaries and we provide firewall rules.

[00:03:10] Jordan: Audit logs — our compliance team wants immutable logs for request/response metadata, user actions, and admin events. Retention 7 years is ideal for certain records. Can Redwood provide that level?
[00:03:23] Maya: We capture detailed audit logs with event types (API calls, user management, model deploys). Logs can be exported to your S3 logs bucket or SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch/other adapters. Retention policies are configurable; for hosted we retain a default window but can arrange long-term export to customer storage for long retention.
[00:03:41] Priya: Is the content of request/response included in logs by default? That's sensitive.
[00:03:45] Tom: By default request metadata and response metadata are logged; full request/response bodies are redacted unless explicitly enabled for debugging with proper controls. For the hosted offering, we redact PII by default. If you run Dedicated/Private you can opt to persist full logs locally and manage retention.

[00:04:20] Priya: Regarding RBAC — we need fine-grained roles so developers can't access production keys or ciphertext. What's the RBAC model?
[00:04:27] Tom: We support RBAC that maps to roles (admin, operator, dev, read-only) and you can integrate with your IdP via SAML + SCIM provisioning. We also support resource-level permissions (per-model or per-route) in Dedicated/Private. Hosted has role layering but resource-level perms are more constrained.
[00:04:47] Marcus: SCIM: does Redwood support automated provisioning and deprovisioning?
[00:04:50] Tom: Yes, SCIM is supported for SSO-enabled customers. We sync users and groups from Okta/Azure AD.

[00:05:15] Jordan: Data residency — some of our data must remain in us-east-1. Can hosted guarantee region pinning?
[00:05:21] Maya: For Hosted we have region options and can pin workloads to regions in some enterprise plans; Dedicated gives you dedicated GPU pools in the region you choose; Private lets you run wherever you like. We'll need to map - depending on account tier we can guarantee region placement in the agreement.

[00:05:44] Priya: Encryption at rest — is server-side encryption AES-256? Does Redwood have BYOK (bring your own key)?
[00:05:50] Tom: SSE is AES-256 for our default, and BYOK via KMS CMKs is supported. For hosted default KMS is Redwood-managed, but we can arrange CMKs with proper contracts for heightened controls.

[00:06:10] Jordan: In terms of evidence, we need the SOC2 report and the control mapping to our security questionnaire.
[00:06:14] Maya: We'll share the SOC 2 Type II and a control map that maps Redwood controls to typical security questionnaire items.

[00:06:29] Marcus: About model caching / KV cache — we want to ensure no persistent leakage between tenants. How is multi-tenancy isolated?
[00:06:36] Tom: We isolate tenant workloads at orchestration level; KV cache is per-customer and keyed per-tenant; it's not shared. I will note the transcript sometimes shows "K V cash" in auto-transcription — but it's per-tenant and TTL/eviction policies can be configured.
[00:06:52] Priya: For the audit trail, can we get signed logs?
[00:06:56] Tom: We provide log signing via integration with your KMS for Dedicated/Private. For hosted we provide tamper-evident logs and export to your archive where you can apply additional signing.

[00:07:20] Jordan: Who has access to customer plaintext in hosted? Are support engineers able to view unredacted requests?
[00:07:26] Maya: By default, support cannot access full plaintext without a documented request and role-based approvals. We have an access request process with time-limited access, audit trail, and approvals. Full plaintext access is rare and logged.
[00:07:40] Priya: We need an SLA around incident response for security incidents.
[00:07:44] Tom: Enterprise plans include incident response SLAs and a dedicated customer success/security contact. We'll include the incident response playbook in the packet.

[00:08:05] Marcus: For Dedicated capacity, how is patching and maintenance handled?
[00:08:09] Tom: For Dedicated we manage the runtime and apply security patches in maintenance windows; we coordinate with customers for rollouts. For Private on-prem, we provide patch bundles and guidance; customers can run updates on their cadence.

[00:08:35] Jordan: Can you do penetration test evidence or allow third-party pentests?
[00:08:39] Maya: We do internal pentests and engage third parties annually; we can share summary reports under NDA. For Private deployments, customers can run their own pentests against their environment.

[00:08:55] Priya: A question on data deletion — we need an API or process for data deletion and proof of deletion for audit.
[00:09:02] Tom: Yes, we support data lifecycle APIs to purge customer data; we can provide deletion receipts and attestations. For hosted, deletion follows our job queue with documented retention timelines; for Dedicated/Private you control deletion directly.

[00:09:30] Jordan: Are retention policies per-workload?
[00:09:33] Tom: Yes, retention can be configured per-route or per-model.

[00:09:45] Marcus: Cost / performance trade-offs: if we enable full request logging + long retention, what's the cost impact?
[00:09:51] Maya: There is added storage and egress cost for exporting and long retention. Our Optimize team can provide recommendations for TTL, sampling rates, and aggregation to balance compliance and cost.

[00:10:15] Priya: Identity proofing — do you support MFA for admin access and enforcement of device posture?
[00:10:20] Tom: We enforce SSO MFA if IdP requires it; for device posture we can integrate with certain IdP features but device posture is typically managed by the customer IdP.

[00:10:40] Jordan: For the pilot we want to test a subset of our workload with encryption keys in our KMS and measure 99th percentile latency and cost per token. Can Redwood support that?
[00:10:50] Maya: Yes. Pilot options: hosted with CMK, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private. We'll scope a pilot with dataset, target SLOs, and a runbook.

[00:11:10] Priya: Any limitations on tokenization or PII redaction we should know about?
[00:11:15] Tom: We provide built-in content redaction tools and recommend a pre-processing step in prod to scrub PII. For some advanced cases we recommend Dedicated or Private so the pipeline stays within your network.

[00:11:40] Marcus: Regarding support for compliance questions, will you assign a solutions engineer to help populate our security questionnaire?
[00:11:46] Maya: Yes, we commonly help customers with the questionnaire. We'll share a control mapping doc and our security pack.

[00:12:05] Jordan: Could you share the list of sub-processors and where logs are stored?
[00:12:10] Maya: We'll send the sub-processor list; logs for hosted may transit through cloud provider logging services but we can provide an export to your storage.

[00:12:30] Tom: (short demo note) For SAML integration, we support metadata upload and SSO auto-provisioning via SCIM. I will send a SAML metadata example and steps to configure with Okta.

[00:12:55] Priya: We have a requirement to rotate keys every 90 days. Is that supported?
[00:12:59] Tom: We support periodic key rotation for CMKs; rotation can be automated in AWS KMS and we can wire up rotation with a minimal maintenance window.

[00:13:20] Jordan: Can I get an audit of all admin actions for the last 6 months?
[00:13:24] Maya: Yes, we can export admin action logs. For hosted we will need a request and will export to a secure bucket; for Dedicated/Private you have direct access.

[00:13:45] Marcus: Service isolation: if we roll with Dedicated, are there noisy neighbor concerns across our reserved pool?
[00:13:51] Tom: Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity for your workloads; we still shard per-tenant but you're isolated to your pool which reduces noisy neighbor effects.

[00:14:10] Jordan: About legal — data processing agreement and standard contractual clauses.
[00:14:13] Maya: We have a DPA template and SCCs as needed; we'll include them in the packet.

[00:14:30] Priya: Can we get a list of encryption algorithms and FIPS support?
[00:14:34] Tom: We support FIPS-compliant cryptography in Dedicated/Private; default AES-256 and TLS 1.2/1.3. We'll include specifics in the security pack.

[00:14:55] Marcus: Observability — does Redwood provide per-route telemetry including cost/latency per-token broken down by model?
[00:15:01] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console includes token-level cost and latency breakdowns and tracing hooks. We can provide exported metrics if necessary.

[00:15:22] Jordan: For the pilot we'll need a contract addendum for CMK usage and a short-term NDA for SOC2 report.
[00:15:28] Maya: We'll send the NDA and an addendum for CMK and pilot terms.

[00:15:40] Priya: Are there any known gaps in Redwood's compliance for finance? Anything you can't do today?
[00:15:46] Tom: We don't have ISO 27001 currently; we also require some engineering work for fully automated long-term archival with signed logs for hosted customers — but for Dedicated/Private those are solved. We'll document the gap and remediation path.

[00:16:10] Jordan: How do you handle backups of models and data?
[00:16:14] Tom: Backups of model artifacts and customer metadata are managed; backups are encrypted and we can provide the backup schedule. For Private you manage backups.

[00:16:30] Maya: Quick recap — we'll send SOC2, control map, SAML/SCIM guide, network diagram, Dedicated pricing, and NDA.
[00:16:39] Jordan: Great. One more — will we be able to bring our own models into Redwood Dedicated?
[00:16:45] Tom: Yes, customers can bring models, we support a model catalog for onboarding and runtime validation; we will need an onboarding checklist for model artifacts.

[00:17:02] Priya: For long-term audit retention, you mentioned exporting logs to S3. Is there any limitation on format or encryption?
[00:17:08] Tom: We can export in JSON/AVRO/CSV formats and server-side encryption with CMK can be enforced for the bucket.

[00:17:30] Jordan: Are there throttles for exports or retrievals?
[00:17:34] Maya: Exports are subject to account quotas; for large exports we can coordinate a one-off job.

[00:17:50] Marcus: Any rate limits that could impact our throughput during peaks?
[00:17:54] Tom: Rate limits are configurable with Dedicated reserved throughput; hosted has burst limits. We'll share throughput options in the pilot terms.

[00:18:15] Priya: Does Redwood provide a compliance contact for audits and security questionnaires?
[00:18:20] Maya: Yes, we have a security contact and you'll get a packet with the contact info.

[00:18:40] Jordan: If we go to Dedicated, can we get a dedicated account manager?
[00:18:44] Maya: Yes enterprise accounts include a CSM and solutions support.

[00:18:58] Marcus: Any client references in fintech?
[00:19:02] Maya: We can share references under NDA, a few financial customers on Dedicated.

[00:19:20] Jordan: Ok let's talk timeline — we want pilot in October and production by end of Q1 '26 ideally.
[00:19:27] Maya: That seems reasonable. Pilot scope and contract terms will determine exact dates.

[00:19:40] Priya: A minor nit — do you have a way to redact specific sensitive fields server-side automatically?
[00:19:46] Tom: We have pre-built redaction rules and can work with your team on custom rules.

[00:20:05] Jordan: Who is responsible for model weights security if we bring our own model?
[00:20:10] Tom: If you bring your own model and run on Dedicated we encrypt model artifacts at rest and manage access via RBAC and KMS. For Private you control the artifact storage.

[00:20:30] Marcus: Any constraints on GPU types or drivers for Private?
[00:20:34] Tom: We have a supported hardware matrix. We'll share it; some kernels require specific drivers for perf.

[00:20:50] Maya: We'll do the follow-ups in a packet and set a time for the technical deep dive. Anything else?
[00:20:58] Jordan: Not from me, thanks.
[00:21:00] Priya: Nothing else, thanks.
[00:21:02] Marcus: All good.

[00:21:05] Maya: Great — next steps as discussed. Thanks everyone.
